newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRA rebound lifts Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: CRA rebound lifts Australian stocks at open.

text.p: The Australian share market opened higher on Friday as a rebound in major miner CRA led the resources sector and the overall market higher.
The All Ordinaries index was up 8.1 points at 2,244.7.
September share price index futures rose 12 points to 2,248, a 3.3 point premium to the underlying index.

After being sold down heavily on concerns over metals prices and profit downgrades, the major miners made a comeback, in particular CRA after its first half net profit of A$714 million (US$552 million) and its upbeat outlook for non-ferrous metals.
"CRA is bouncing back from its weakness of the last couple of days," said broker Tony Russell of Morgan Stockbroking.
"Our market has lanquished on the back of downgrades in BHP and CRA while the U.S. has had several strong days. Now you have seen the selling in those stocks dissipate," he said.
Expectations were for some gains to hold with the market showing a reasonably firm tone. "I expect gains of five to 10 points by the end of the day," Russell said.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about two to one, while about 40 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
